title: Log Watchdog: choose the console
question: Both primary directions preserve your incident-first workflow. Choose a layout to develop, or steer the direction.

options.label: Event recorder
options.lineage: Flight event recorders and instrument traces
options.thesis: Follow one incident along a shared timeline from signal to evidence to delivery.
options.viewport: Active incident strip above a wide error-log chart; aligned evidence and delivery records below.
options.risk: The timeline must remain readable when timestamps become dense.

raised.raise: A selected interval synchronizes every evidence view.
Color marks meaningful signals; uncertainty stays explicit.
The active incident holds still while secondary context recedes.
Observed and expected values share precision and units.
Logs and attempts use consistent timestamp alignment.
Four clear destinations keep navigation bounded.

options.label: Incident workbench
options.lineage: Operations dispatch desks and debugger workspaces
options.thesis: Keep the incident queue and its evidence visible together.
options.viewport: Active incidents lead a wide workspace, with a persistent evidence pane and service trends underneath.
options.risk: Familiar and efficient, but less distinctive than the event recorder.

options.label: Drawcord cape
options.thesis: Evidence panels gather around a selected incident.
materials: reference grammar translated into console structure
options.viewport: Evidence panels gather around a selected incident.
options.case: Declined on audience identification and product clarity: Metaphorical controls slow operational scanning.
options.kept: A selected interval synchronizes every evidence view.

canonCard.thesis: A standard service dashboard with an incident table, executed precisely.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, summary metrics, trend chart, and incident list.
canonCard.risk: Familiar, with less emphasis on the connected evidence trail.
